newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares climb to another life peak.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares climb to another life peak.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange charged ahead to a record high for the fourth consecutive day on Monday but turnover was moderate because of market holidays in Britain and the United States.
The Oslo bourse Total index finished at 1,165.19 points, up 0.93 percent from Friday's record close in trade worth 982 million crowns. It touched an intra-day high of 1,166.05 points.
Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner outperformed the market, its A share soaring 4.88 percent to 430 crowns in trade worth 80 million crowns.
The B share was up 4.81 percent at 392 crowns.
Several analysts have upgraded their forecasts on Kvaerner since the company presented first-quarter profits earlier this month that beat market expectations.
Brokers said a strong economic outlook in Europe had helped boost cyclical shares such as forestry group Norske Skog and metals maker Elkem.
Norske Skog's A share was up 2.86 percent at 252 crowns while Elkem jumped nearly four percent to 145 crowns.
But industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro, Norway's largest listed company, fell 0.6 percent to 361.50 crowns.
